title: SB 549 (108th General Assembly): As introduced, prohibits persons who are not U.S. citizens from being admitted to polling places; requires appointed poll watchers to be U.S. citizens. - Amends TCA Title 2, Chapter 7, Part 1.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.

(e_other_rule)
(section) TCA 2-7-103(a), Section 1
(quote) provided that only citizens of the United States may be admitted to a polling place.
(section) TCA 2-7-103(f), new, Section 2
(quote) Nothing in this section shall permit citizens of any country other than the United States to be admitted to a polling place while the procedures of this chapter 7 are being carried out.
(section) TCA 2-7-104(a), Section 3
(quote) All appointed poll watchers must be citizens of the United States and must have reached the age of seventeen (17) by election day.
(other) Sec 4: effective on becoming law.
(other) Sec 3 also sets a minimum age of 17 for appointed poll watchers.
(other) version: Draft (only version saved): citizens-only admission to polling places and citizen poll watchers (slot e). Senate committee amendment and floor amendment SA0058 (adopted 2013-03-07) are not saved; the Engrossed text is not saved.
(other) note: Rule is about who may enter a polling place and watch; it does not state who may vote or require any proof of citizenship. Passed the Senate and was held on the House desk (2013-03-11); the House took up companion HB985, which also stalled.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
